newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to re-assess GSM licence transfers-minister.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to re-assess GSM licence transfers-minister.

text.p: Turkey's state telecom company, Turk Telekom, will review a plan to demand $500 million for the transfer of its two licences for Global System for Mobiles (GSM) to two local companies, Transport Minister Necdet Menzir said.
"Work has begun to re-assess the value of GSM licence transfers," he told reporters.
"We will complete the work in short time and submit the result to the Council of State," he said.
According to the constitution, The Council of State, top administrative court in Turkey, has to review all state deals involving concessions in strategic products and services.
Turkey allowed Turkcell and Telsim, two local companies with foreign partnerships, to run GSM networks in Turkey in 1993. The two companies pay 65 percent of their income to Turk Telekom.
The former coalition government was seeking $500 million from each company for the transfer of the licences for 25 years as part of the privatisation drive.
But Telekom officials have said the value of the licences was changing and a re-evaluation was necessary.
State Minister Gunes Taner, in charge of economy, said the government would earn between $1 billion and $1.5 billion from the sale of the GSM licences by the end of this year.
Menzir also said the government would not carry out a plan by its predecessor that Turk Telekom would tender for two more digital telephone systems with higher capacities.

Turkcell, which has about 75 percent market share, is joint venture between Finland Telekom with 34 percent, Ericsson with 15 percent and Turkey's private MV Komunikasyon with 14 percent and other smaller shareholders.
Telsim is mainly owned by Rumeli Telefon with 88.39 percent. Motorola and French Alcatel also hold small shares.
Both companies have about 700,000 subcribers in total and their capacities allow for up to 1.5 million mobile telephone users.
